CYBERPUNK.GrappleText: Succeed? Great, now you can try to Hold, Choke or Throw your opponent.

SETTINGS.TrainedSkillsFirstHint: Whether trained skills always come first in the skills list
SETTINGS.CombatAutomationHint: Resolve combat automatically: applied damage, wound statuses and saves, the opposed melee defense, burning wounds, blast and suppression zones. Turn this off and the system only rolls and posts cards — the table applies everything by hand. Combat management stays on either way: initiative, the movement allowance, the pause and turn notifications.
SETTINGS.CombatAutomationMenuHint: The master switch and every optional rule that depends on it.
SETTINGS.DamageApplyModeHint: How damage from an attack card reaches the target. Either way, only a GM client ever writes to the target.
SETTINGS.DamageApplyModeAuto: Automatic, on the active GM's client
SETTINGS.PcSaveModeHint: Who rolls a Stun or Death save for a player character. NPCs always roll automatically.
SETTINGS.PcSaveModeManual: The owner is prompted (30 s, then automatic)
SETTINGS.ArmorAblationHint: Optional rule: worn armor loses a point of SP per hit that gets through it. Recorded on the armor either way; switching this off restores the printed SP.
SETTINGS.SeveranceThresholdHint: Damage to one limb above this, after BTM, severs it; the head kills outright. 0 turns the rule off.
SETTINGS.ActionEconomyHint: Every attack after the first in the same turn takes a cumulative -3. Attacks only: skill rolls, stat rolls and opposed defenses cost nothing. The counter resets at the start of the actor's turn.
SETTINGS.PartyInitiativeHint: Each side rolls one initiative die per round; every combatant still adds their own REF and modifiers.
SETTINGS.DodgeVsRangedHint: House rule, not the corebook: a declared dodge gives ranged attackers -2 against that character until the start of their next turn. The corebook allows dodging melee attacks only. It needs a running encounter — outside a turn order there is no next turn to end it on, so nothing is declared.
SETTINGS.SpreadZoneRoundsHint: How many rounds a drawn shotgun pattern stays on the map. A pattern laid in round 3 with 1 here goes at the start of round 4. 0 leaves it standing until the encounter ends or the GM takes it off.
SETTINGS.BlastZoneRoundsHint: How many rounds a drawn blast crater stays on the map. 0 leaves it standing until the encounter ends or the GM takes it off.
SETTINGS.SweepZoneRoundsHint: How many rounds a drawn flamethrower stream stays on the map. 0 leaves it standing until the encounter ends or the GM takes it off.
SETTINGS.BlockOverspentMovementHint: Refuse a player’s move that would take a token past MA metres walking, or MA x 3 running, in one turn. The GM is never restricted. With this off the ruler still marks the overspend. The allowance is in metres and is compared against the scene's own grid units without converting them: a scene gridded in anything else is the table's own to reconcile.
SETTINGS.TurnSoundHint: Play a sound and show a message when your combatant's turn starts, and when it is next.
SETTINGS.FNFF2EnabledHint: Enable the optional Friday Night Fistfight 2 martial arts ruleset (new styles, actions, and opposed roll flow).

CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.Title: Reflex (Combat)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. You just screw up.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.6: 6. Weapon discharges or strikes something harmless.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.7: 7. Weapon jams, or knocks you to the ground for 1 round.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.9_10: 9–10. You manage to wound a member of your own party.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexAthletics.Title: Reflex (Athletics)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexAthletics.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. You just mess up and make an idiot of yourself.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexAthletics.5_7: 5–7. You fail miserably. Take 1 point in minor damage (sprain, fall, stumble), plus make a Save vs. Stun.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexAthletics.8_10: 8–10. You fail abysmally. If a physical action, take 1D6 in damage from falling or strained muscles. Also make a roll vs Stun at -1.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.Title: Control Loss Table
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.1_2: 1–2. Skid or slew; no other result.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.3_4.Ground: 3–4. Major skid; slide 1D10x10 feet sideways in direction of travel.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.3_4.Aircraf: 3–4. Aircraft stalls, losing 1D10x50 feet of altitude.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.5_6.Ground: 5–6. Roll ground vehicle after sliding 1D10x10 feet sideways in direction of travel; take 5D6 damage.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.5_6.Aircraf: 5–6. Aircraft goes into spin, lose 1D10x100 feet of altitude.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Tech.Title: Tech (Repair or create)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Tech.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. You just can't get it together.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Tech.5_7: 5–7. You not only fail, you make it worse! You drop the tools you're working with, or you lose your grip and damage the thing you're working with even more. Raise the Difficulty by 5 points and try again.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Tech.8_10: 8–10. Wow. Did you ever blow it! You damaged the device or creation beyond repair. Buy a new one.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Emp.Title: EMP (Convince, Fast talk, Seduce)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Emp.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. They just won't buy it.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Emp.5_6: 5–6. So much for your people skills. You not only don't convince them; you leave them totally cold (-4 to your next EMP die roll) to any other suggestion you might have.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Emp.7_10: 7–10. Yow! You blew it royally. You not only didn't convince them, but now they're actually violently opposed to anything you want to do. Roll 1D10. On a 1–4, they actually attempt to do you physical harm.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.EmpExtra.1_4: they actually attempt to do you physical harm.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.EmpExtra.5_10: they are violently opposed and resist you.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Int.Title: INT (Figure out, Notice, catch a clue)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Int.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. You just don't know how to do it. You don't know what's going on. You carry on, oblivious to higher concerns.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Int.5_7: 5–7. You don't know anything about what's going on and you haven't a clue about how to do anything about it. Make a Convince check at -2 to see if anyone else notices how dumb you are.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Int.8_10: 8–10. Wow, are you oblivious. You not only don't know what's going on or anything about the subject, but everyone knows how ignorant you are.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.AutoWeaponOnlyJam: Automatic weapons: fumble table is ignored; only a Reliability jam check is made.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReliabilityResult.NoJam: lucky you, it didn’t jam - just a misfire
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.DischargeApplied: Result: the weapon discharged (ammo is now 0).
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.DischargeNotApplied: Result: lucky you, it didn’t discharge - just a misfire
CYBERPUNK.AmmoQuantityHint: Computed from boxes and loose rounds. Set «Per box» first.
CYBERPUNK.AmmoLooseHint: The remainder of rounds from the box already opened — what the total has left over once the full boxes are counted out.
CYBERPUNK.AmmoDamageFormulaHint: The round carries its own damage and it replaces the weapon's — the book prints one per shotgun gauge (10ga. 5D6+3, 12ga. 4D6+2, 20ga. 3D6+1). Leave it empty and the weapon's own damage is rolled.
CYBERPUNK.AmmoPenHalvesHint: An AP round meets half the armor's SP and then has what gets through divided — 0.5 in both armor multipliers, 2 in the divisor. Each box decides whether the division applies against that class of armor; turn both off and there is no division at all.
CYBERPUNK.AmmoSlugHint: A finned slug has normal AP ability against all armors, and the damage that penetrates hard armor is not halved — leave the hard armor box clear. Armor-piercing, Slug and Mono edge are one family: a round carries one of them, never two.
CYBERPUNK.AmmoMonoHint: A mono edge cuts armor instead of punching through it: SP counts as one third against soft armor and two thirds against hard, and the damage that gets through is not halved. The book states the fractions, so there is nothing here to set.
CYBERPUNK.AmmoStunOnHitHint: A hit demands a Stun Save, and the save number drops 2 for every successive shot within three combat rounds. Unless the charge ignores armor, only a hit that got past the armor asks for one.
CYBERPUNK.AmmoDoTDamageHint: One damage formula per burning turn, so a fire can decline the way the corebook's own do — a flamethrower is 2D10, then 1D10, then 1D6. Leave a turn empty or at 0 and it deals nothing that turn, which is how a fire burns, smoulders, then flares.
CYBERPUNK.AmmoOverallBodyHint: Explosives and molotovs damage the overall body rather than a hit location: the Torso's armor meets the whole blast, and there is no location roll, no doubled head hit, no severance and no cyberlimb absorption. Grenades are location-silent in the rules, so leave this off for them.
CYBERPUNK.AmmoSpreadDamageHint: Empty — the weapon's damage. 0 — no damage.
SETTINGS.ReloadByMagazinesHint: If enabled, reloading always consumes a full magazine (weapon capacity). If disabled, only missing rounds are consumed.
SETTINGS.PlayersCanEditCyberwareHumanity: If enabled, players who can edit a cyberware item can also edit its Humanity Cost and Humanity Loss fields. If disabled, only the GM can edit those fields.
SETTINGS.ShowInlineRollFormulaHint: If enabled, damage roll tooltips show the formula, numeric modifiers, final result, and dice. If disabled, only dice are shown.
CYBERPUNK.AmmoItemNotFoundReloadedLegacy: Ammo item not found. Reloaded without ammo tracking.
